voice.title: Voice
voice.mic.none: No microphone found: voice is off.
voice.speaker: Windows voice: {0}
voice.vcredist: Speech recognition needs the free “Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable” ({0}): install it from aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.{0}.exe and restart AL-76. The AL-76 installer will bring it by itself.
setup.welcome.text: A voice assistant that lives on your PC. The name comes from an Isaac Asimov story: a robot lost on Earth, whom the man who finds him simply calls "Al". You can call me that too: "{0}".
setup.welcome.f1: I answer by voice or in writing, open apps and folders, set timers and reminders
setup.welcome.f2: I help with study and work, kept in separate areas
setup.welcome.f3: Speech recognition stays on the PC; you choose the brain
setup.welcome.note: A few steps and you're ready. Every step can be skipped, and every choice can be changed later in Settings.
lang.restart: The language changes the next time {0} starts.
setup.you.text: What you write here goes into my instructions, so the answers fit you.
setup.you.name: Your name
setup.you.address.custom: Or write your own (e.g. boss, your name)
setup.you.address.note: With no title I call you neither "sir" nor by name: I just answer.
setup.you.city: City, for the weather (empty = where you connect from)
setup.you.privacy: They stay on this PC. With a cloud brain they reach its provider together with your questions.
setup.study.text: Knowing what you study and your job, I answer better and keep your commitments apart.
setup.study.label: What and where you study
setup.study.note: Exams and dates can be said aloud too: "remember that the Statistics exam is on 20 January".
setup.work.label: Your job, and its hours
setup.work.hint: e.g. office clerk, Monday to Friday 9 to 6
setup.studywork.none: With the "Other" profile there is nothing to write here: go on.
setup.areas.text: Reminders, calendar and memory are split into areas, so study does not mix with work.
setup.areas.note: You can switch by voice too: "switch to work".
setup.brain.text: Simple things (time, timers, apps, reminders, weather) I do by myself at once. For real questions I use a brain: a local one, free and private, or Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini with a subscription or account you already have, with no API to pay.
brain.auto.title: Automatic
brain.auto.detail: The first one ready among Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and the local model.
brain.local.title: Local model
brain.local.detail: Gemma with Ollama, on this PC: free and private. Needs a Medium or High tier PC.
brain.claude.detail: Claude subscription (Pro or Max), through Claude Code.
brain.chatgpt.detail: ChatGPT subscription (Plus or Pro), through OpenAI's Codex.
brain.gemini.detail: Google account (free Gemini or a subscription), through Antigravity CLI.
brain.status.prepare: Installed: it must be prepared for {0}
brain.status.ollama.missing: Ollama does not answer: not installed or not running
brain.status.ollama.model: Ollama running, the {0} model is missing
brain.status.ollama.none: This PC is Base tier: no local model, only cloud brains and instant commands
brain.console.note: The buttons open a PowerShell window with the official command written below. Follow the instructions (signing in happens in the browser), then come back and press "Check again".
brain.gemini.note: On its own Antigravity runs commands and writes files. "Prepare" adds rules to its settings that allow only {0}'s tools: no terminal, no edits, no web pages (they apply when you use agy yourself too).
brain.privacy: With a cloud brain, your questions and what is needed to answer go to that provider. You can switch by voice too: "use ChatGPT", "switch to Gemini", "back to the local model", "ask Claude…".
setup.perm.text: Windows lets me do only what you allow. Here is what each permission is for: give the ones you want; they are removed in Windows Settings › Privacy & security.
perm.mic.why: To hear the call and your commands. Needed for the voice; the audio stays on the PC.
perm.notify.why: To show timers and reminders when the sound is off too.
perm.startup.why: So I'm ready as soon as you turn on the PC. No administrator rights.
perm.control.why: On Windows no permission is needed to press buttons and type in other apps: I do it only when you ask, and never in password managers, banks, Windows Settings and terminals.
setup.voice.text: Call me with the wake phrase, then say what you need.
voice.name: Assistant's name
voice.call.note: Two or three words you don't say by chance. Applies from the next start.
voice.engine.auto: Automatic: Kokoro on Medium and High PCs, the Windows voice on Base PCs
voice.try: Try it: say "{0}" in a normal voice.
voice.notready: The voice is still getting ready: the test works as soon as it is listening.
setup.modules.text: Niche parts stay off until you switch them on: that keeps the brains' instructions short and quick.
setup.done.text: Here is what I learnt. Everything can be changed in Settings, and this setup can be reopened from the menu in the notification area.
setup.done.ex2: "{0}, remind me to call Mark tomorrow at 9"
setup.sum.name: Your name is {0}
setup.sum.nomic: Microphone not allowed: the voice will not work
confirm.text: When I ask for a yes before acting.
confirm.essential.detail: I ask only before purchases, passwords, email, programs to run and unknown sites. The rest I do at once.
confirm.careful.detail: I also ask before sending messages, deleting, closing apps and overwriting files.
apps.control.switch: Read and use the other apps and look at the screen
apps.control.detail: Buttons, fields, keys and scrolling in other apps' windows; a picture of the front window or of the screen when you ask. The local model never uses it.
apps.control.never: Never in password managers, banks, Windows Settings, terminals or the registry editor; never in password fields. "Stop" halts everything at once.
notes.folders.hint: Folders, one per line (empty: Documents\Appunti and Documents\Notes)
notes.folders.note: AL-76 searches inside the PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and text files of these folders, all on the PC. Other folders stay out. Scanned pages are read with the Windows OCR while the PC is plugged in. New folders are read on the next round, within 6 hours or at restart.
system.restart.note: Language, name and wake phrase apply after a restart.
system.data.note: Memory, reminders, settings and logs: all in this folder, on the PC.
hud.webview.missing: The sphere needs Microsoft Edge WebView2, which this PC lacks. AL-76 still works by voice; WebView2 installs from microsoft.com/edge/webview2.
nucleus.menu.bubble.voice: Speech bubble for spoken answers too
look.intro: How you see me on screen.
look.nucleus.note: The small window that stays when you shrink the sphere (double click on the sphere). Click to open the sphere again, drag to move it.
look.backdrop.note: Off, it blends with the wallpaper; on, it stays readable on light wallpapers or over windows.
look.robot.walks: Strolls along the bottom edge while waiting
look.robot.note: Click: a pat · double click: the sphere · drag to move it. Dropped or thrown towards the bottom right corner, it goes back to the edge and strolls.
look.robot.missing: The 3D model is missing: the robot is not part of {0}. Put scene.gltf (with scene.bin and the textures folder) in {1}. Until then you see the satellite.
areas.schedule.hint: One line per area, for example "Work: mon-fri 9-18" or "Study: mon, wed, fri 15-19". When a slot starts AL-76 switches to that area by itself; a switch by voice lasts until the next slot. Empty: by voice only.
areas.schedule.bad: Lines not understood (area or hours missing): {0}
areas.briefing.why: After the first request of the day, between {0} and {1}: weather, appointments and reminders of the active area.
accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.text: Calendar, reminders, mail and contacts can stay on this PC or in a Microsoft or Google account. You sign in in the browser: AL-76 never sees the password, and you can take the permissions back whenever you like.
accounts.browser: The browser opened: sign in and accept. You have 5 minutes.
accounts.guide.microsoft: How to get the ID (once, free): portal.azure.com › App registrations › New registration; account types: "any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts"; redirect URI: "Public client/native" with http://localhost. Paste the "Application (client) ID" here.
accounts.guide.google: How to get ID and secret (once, free): console.cloud.google.com › new project; enable Google Calendar API, Tasks API, Gmail API and People API; OAuth consent screen: external, testing, add your address as a test user; Credentials › Create OAuth client ID › "Desktop app". Paste ID and secret here.
accounts.areas.note: For each area: this PC, Microsoft or Google; then the name of the calendar and of the reminder list in that account (empty: the main ones).
accounts.mail.note: AL-76 reads and searches the unread mail; to send one it always asks for a spoken yes.
study.timetable.note: The subscription link your school or university gives for its calendar. You can also dictate the timetable ("Monday Calculus 9 to 11") or have it read from a PDF or a photo.
study.evening.why: Once a day, at the chosen hour: how long you studied and worked, what is left for the week.
university.saved: Credentials saved, encrypted on this PC
university.name: University name
university.server: Address of the student app's server
university.agent: App User-Agent (if the server requires it)
university.both: Username and password are both needed.
university.note: Read only: lessons, agenda, career, notices. Enrolling, signing and accepting grades are not possible. The credentials go only to that server.
maker.folders: Folders with Arduino sketches, one per line (empty: Documents\Arduino, Documents and Projects)
maker.arduino.note: Needs Arduino IDE 2 (it contains arduino-cli) or arduino-cli. AL-76 lists the connected boards, compiles, uploads and reads the serial port.
maker.printer.host: Bambu Lab printer address (shown on the printer, e.g. 10.0.0.50)
maker.printer.note: On the printer: Settings › Network › LAN mode, where address and code are shown. AL-76 only reads the status and tells you when a print ends, pauses or fails.
maker.ros.note: ROS 2 in WSL2 or on another computer: start "ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml" there. AL-76 lists topics, reads and publishes messages, calls services.
maker.robot.note: In Robot Console: Diagnostics and ROS2 › Python API › Start local API, then Copy token. Every run on the real robot is still approved in Robot Console.
phone.restart: The phone link starts the next time AL-76 starts.
phone.how: On the iPhone or iPad open the AL-76 app and scan this QR code, or type the code below and the PC's address.
phone.note: Works on the home network and on Tailscale, never from the internet; the code never travels over the network. The phone finds the PC by itself. The first time Windows asks to let AL-76 use the network: choose Private networks. The phone can see the PC screen and click and type on it, only while that view is open.
phone.version: The phone app is newer than AL-76 on the PC: update AL-76.
typebar.hint: Type a request and press Enter; Esc closes
tray.desktoplink.done: AL-76 shortcut created on the desktop.
voiceprint.title: Recognising your voice
voiceprint.text: AL-76 learns what your voice sounds like from a few sentences read aloud, so it can ignore the TV, videos and other people. It stays on this PC: it is numbers, the audio is not kept.
voiceprint.mode.off.detail: Answers anyone who says the call.
voiceprint.mode.observe.detail: Checks the voice and writes it in the log, but answers everyone (to try it).
voiceprint.notready: The microphone is not ready yet.
voiceprint.nomodel: The voiceprint model does not load.
voiceprint.read: Read the sentence below aloud, then pause briefly.
voiceprint.done.title: Done
voiceprint.done: There are now {0} recorded sentences. You can close the window.
projects.folders.hint: Project folders, one per line (empty = Projects, source\repos, Documents\GitHub and Documents\Projects)
news.sources: Sources, one per line as "Name | RSS feed address" (empty = the default ones)
news.topics: Topics you care about, one per line (they go first)
news.briefing.detail: Three headlines at the end of the briefing, if they arrive within 5 seconds.
tv.host: Name or address of the Samsung TV on the network (e.g. Samsung.local; empty = no TV)
tv.note: The first time the TV asks on screen whether to trust AL-76: choose Allow. To turn it on from off it must have been seen on at least once.
maker.lab: ROS 2 lab folder with pixi.toml (for "start the lab")
owner.check.detail: To open programs or scripts and to forget memories, after the yes face, fingerprint or PIN is needed too. Without Windows Hello set up the yes is enough.
